comments.value: We are not considering this kind of system or policy at this time.

details:
I would love an official system created by VRChat, that gives mod creators the ability to send in their code to the appropriate Developers to be reviewed, optimized, and officially integrated into their platform.  I am sure you already are picking up on many problems, so I will expand on how realistic I believe some things are, and much elaboration.
The first thing you will likely notice, is that modifications are not allowed in the first place to the Client and Platform (See Section 4 & 11 of VRC TOS).  Mod creators certainly have to break TOS in order to make any mods.  Why would VRChat ever want to set up a system that directly clashes with their own Terms of Service?  That, in a way, encourages people to break the rules?  I will be attempting to reason and justify why they would ever consider that.
I believe mod creators will always persist to some degree for this game, and every other.  I also believe there is a decently sizable amount of the community who are currently benefiting from mods.  I am not gonna throw out some random made up statistics, but there are about 46k total members of the VRChat Modding Group Discord server, and 62k in the EMM (Source, a discord invite link gives the active and total member count).  And no, I do not advocate using any of the mods they offer from any server.  The Official VRChat server has 200k+ total members, and way more people just play the game and don’t even join the discord, but tens of thousands of people are still considerable.  What I do know for sure is that every single person in the community could benefit from the features, QoL, and bug fixes many mods provide that could be officially integrated into the platform.  I want everyone to be able to benefit from the good things these mods are doing, and make it easier for the Devs to implement them.
The modifications that would be sent to this hypothetical system would be for additional features, QoL, bugs, or an improvement on an existing functionality.  I do understand posts can already be made on VRChat’s feedback boards, but this could be an alternate, more direct way to get things through.  I can say with certainty that any mods malicious in nature on the surface level would be swiftly considered and appropriately denied by the Devs and therefore do not need to be worried about.  When I say malicious, I mean mods that make the experience of other players worse.  For example, a mod that enables the feature to crash people, or one that could disable all the colliders in a world.  You may worry malicious code could snuck into seemingly normal mods that find itself into the game.  When I say malicious here, I mean something that would send and receive sensitive information to said malicious person, or something similar.  I feel the Devs who work on the client would easily be able to pick out anything bad given they built it themselves.  But, I am certainly not a Dev nor modder, so it may be immensely more complicated than it seems.
Unfortunately the code submitted by the MC will NOT just be ready for official integration into the client.  Even if the code is well made and optimized, it will need to be changed in some capacity in order for it to comply with every part of the platform’s code, and that it will not break as the game updates.  This will take a considerable amount of resources from the Devs who work on the client, server, or even the web or unity Engineers. I worry very much that VRChat may lack those resources to spend. 
I do not believe the moderation system has to change after the implementation of this.  Mods should still be moderated the same way.  Many mod creators still modify this game regardless of the rules.  Let me stress that the purpose of this argument is NOT to allow mods.  It is to benefit the entire community including the Devs off the work of mod creators.  
I do not believe mod creators should get financial compensation for successfully submitting a mod.  The staff members of the VRCMG & EMM Discord do not believe in paid mods, nor do the creators of the mods they deem “finished”.  A message was made in October 2020 in the VRCMG in #announcements by staff that all of their software is free.  It is a year old, but so far I do not see anything officially posted that conflicts with that statement.  Regardless, I think it is reasonable to conclude from that message and many others that most modders would not have a problem submitting their code without receiving money.
I personally believe there is net gain to be had from a system like this to be implemented, or similar.  I am tired of seeing arguments between modders and non-modders getting basically nowhere, so I want to try bringing up something that can actually be argued.  I do not think the Devs find this topic to be high priority to them at the moment, but I still want to write about this anyway.  
Questions that NEED to be considered that I cannot answer before this could be implemented:
1.)  Would it take more time & resources for the Devs to understand, review, revise, and edit the codes of mods submitted than to just take the idea of the mod and create it from scratch?
2.)  Would this require a considerable change to the TOS?
3.)  Would this cause a problem with current and future investors?
4.)  Would this cause many more people to use mods that have not been officially integrated yet?  Or maybe it might cause some to not even use mods anymore when their favorite features already have been officially integrated?
title: Modification Submission for Official VRC Integration
